analysis:
Examined the `SandboxSetupProgress.swift` diff, the new `SandboxSlotChange.swift` and the `SandboxSetupTests.swift` patch. Only the `confirm` change is production behavior in the modified file; the rest is the unchanged installer-event parser/renderer.

The `SandboxSlotChange` struct is pure comparison logic over the add-on's status and plan. `applying(to:)` copies the plan's counts into explicit `--linux-slots`/`--macos-slots` options. The counts come from the add-on's own `--plan` output, an integer parse with no shell interpolation here. `command` and `headline` interpolate only Ints and `Sandbox.cli`, so there is no injection.

The tests show the intended flow. On rerun, setup downloads install.sh and runs `--plan`. A prompt (default Y) is shown on a terminal. Without a prompt, setup applies only a plan that adds slots. `--force` is never passed, so running jobs are not stopped. If jobs are running, setup skips the plan. The installer's exit status 4 is surfaced.

The rerun path now fetches and executes the installer on already-installed Macs, rather than only on first setup. It rests on the same trust as T-061 (TLS to the sandbox service, add-on release verification). It is not a new trust class, but it is more frequent execution as the owner (A-019). The new unattended auto-apply of add-only plans is also bounded by the installer's own refusal while jobs run.

The real `SandboxSetupFlow`, `SandboxAddonStatus` and the installer download/verification code were not supplied. I could not verify when the prompt is shown, whether `interactiveInput` gates it, or how the installer script is authenticated. Both integration points need a look. No inference, attestation or coordinator boundary is touched.

findings.detail: `SandboxTerminal.confirm` now takes `defaultYes`, and head line 463 returns true when `defaultYes && answer.isEmpty`. `readInput()` returns nil at EOF (Ctrl-D, closed or exhausted stdin), and `?? ""` turns that into an empty answer. With `defaultYes: true`, EOF therefore counts as approval, not just an Enter keypress. The new rerun prompt in `SandboxSetupTests` uses this default-yes path. That prompt can offer a plan that removes slots, and applying it runs the downloaded installer as the Mac owner (TB-013/T-061 surface). A closed stdin or a scripted pipe could silently apply the change, and a removal would be applied with no explicit `y`. Fix: treat a nil read as no, and apply the default only to an explicit empty line, for example `guard let line = readInput() else { return false }`. The flow that decides when the prompt is shown is not in the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Default-yes confirm treats EOF/closed stdin as consent to apply an installer slot change
